newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian British bank to issue bonds for $29 mln.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian British bank to issue bonds for $29 mln.

text.p: Private-sector Egyptian British Bank said on Saturday it was offering investors 100 million pounds ($29.41 million) worth of five-year non-convertible bonds from December 15.

The bank, in which HSBC Holdings own a 40 percent stake, said each of the 10,000 bonds was worth 1,000 pounds. The offer is valid for two months but if the issue is covered, the bank can close it after 10 days.
The bonds have a 0.25 percent coupon and yields would be distributed every three months, the bank said.
Bond yields will be based on the latest annualised average yield of 91-day treasury bills announced by the Central Bank no more than 14 days before the bond yield is calculated.

If the Central Bank stops issuing 91-day treasury bills or does not announce a yield within the specified time, the bond yield will equal the bank's discount rate -- currently at 13.25 percent -- less 3.25 percent.
Investors must pay a 2.50 pound handling fee and if the offer is oversubscribed, bonds will be distributed on a pro rata basis.

The bank said it would use the 100 million pounds raised by the issue to finance its activities. Egyptian British Bank also said it made a net profit for the first six months of calendar 1996 of 9.699 million. Profits for 1995 were 17.007 million.

It forecast total 1996 profits would rise to 19.093 million, 21.534 in 1997, 29.887 in 1998, 35.096 million in 1999, 47.544 million in 2000 and that they would be 62.103 million in 2001, the year when the bonds mature.
